system.name: AI6P-280 Sacrificial Hello World
system.summary: A web application front end: a React+Vite SPA hosted on AWS Amplify, wired to an AppSync GraphQL API and a Cognito user pool that already exist and are owned OUTSIDE this project. This project provisions no backend infrastructure — its only coupling to the backend is a declared runtime-config contract read from SSM at build time. Bootstrapped from the Product Sweet webapp template (external-backend mode) around one Note vertical slice; replace that slice with the migrated surface and refine this summary as the project takes shape.
system.technology: react-vite, AWS Amplify Hosting, GitHub Actions, AWS SSM Parameter Store (runtime config)

externalSystems.name: GitHub
externalSystems.summary: Source repository hosting at https://github.com/productsweet-bootstrap-e2e-app/ai6p-2160-reconcile-proof. Stores the SPA source, the `.kanban/` task tree, the `.agent/` knowledge folder, and the GitHub Actions workflows committed by the bootstrap. No backend source lives here — the backend is owned elsewhere.

externalSystems.name: GitHub Actions
externalSystems.summary: CI/CD runner federated into AWS via OIDC. Runs the always-on `pr-gate` required check on every PR and the frontend deploy workflow on push to main. There is deliberately NO backend deploy workflow. The frontend build reads this project's declared runtime-config parameters from SSM (`scripts/gen-aws-config.mjs`) and FAILS the build if any is unreadable. Higher environments are promoted by `promote-<env>.yml` workflows dispatched by the Product Sweet webapp with the reviewed commit pinned.

externalSystems.name: AWS Amplify Hosting
externalSystems.summary: Hosts the built SPA on the Amplify CDN with an SPA rewrite rule so deep links fall through to `index.html`. Auto-build on main is disabled; the deploy workflow is the only release path.

externalSystems.name: SSM Runtime Config
externalSystems.summary: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameters under `/productsweet-external-smoke/webapp` holding the external backend's endpoint and Cognito ids. Seeded by the backend's owner / an operator — this project only READS them, at build time, once per deploy. The same paths in different environment accounts hold that environment's values; the deploy role's credentials decide which it reads.

externalSystems.name: Existing GraphQL Backend
externalSystems.summary: The pre-existing AppSync GraphQL API (with its resolvers and data store) that this SPA consumes. Provisioned, deployed, versioned, and operated OUTSIDE this project's boundary. Its schema is a contract this project consumes and cannot change unilaterally.

externalSystems.name: Existing Cognito User Pool
externalSystems.summary: The pre-existing Cognito user pool the SPA authenticates against and the external API authorizes on. Sign-up policy, MFA, custom claims, and the app-client configuration belong to the backend's owner, not this project.

externalSystems.name: App User
externalSystems.summary: An authenticated end user of the web app. Signs in through the existing Cognito user pool and reads / writes Notes through the SPA.

containers.name: Single-Page App
containers.summary: The react-vite SPA served from AWS Amplify Hosting — the ONLY container this project owns. Renders the Note vertical slice as a starting scaffold (sign in, create a note, list Notes) against the existing GraphQL API via the aws-amplify client; a migration replaces that scaffold with the real surface.
containers.technology: React 19 + Vite 6 SPA — single-page app rendered client-side; build emits static `index.html` + JS bundle + assets; aws-amplify client for AppSync GraphQL + Cognito auth
responsibilities: Authenticate users against the existing Cognito user pool

Read its endpoint + Cognito ids from build-time-generated config (never hardcoded)
Serve from AWS Amplify Hosting at https://pending-first-deploy.example/
Render the entire app client-side — every route is served from the same `index.html`; configure the Amplify rewrite rule so deep links fall through to the SPA
